title: Adding Set Items
learningObjectives: Explain adding set items and when it is useful.
Use the relevant Python operations with correct syntax.
Predict the result of common operations and edge cases.
Distinguish mutation, return values and error behavior.
Apply the concept to a small data-processing task.

understand.concept: add inserts one hashable element. update inserts elements from one or more iterables. Re-adding an existing member does not create a duplicate; update treats strings as iterables of characters.
understand.whyItMatters: Adding Set Items is useful when a program needs to organize, inspect or transform related data reliably.
understand.analogy: A set is like a collection of unique membership cards: each item is present once, with no positional promise.
understand.analogyLimit: A set does not preserve a meaningful position for each member, and elements must be hashable.

explain.narrative:
## Adding Set Items

add inserts one hashable element. update inserts elements from one or more iterables. Re-adding an existing member does not create a duplicate; update treats strings as iterables of characters.

## Choosing an operation

Read the example code and check whether the operation mutates the object, returns a new value, or may raise an exception. Use membership tests and defaults where input may be missing.

## Practical reasoning

The five examples progress from basic use to a small real-world pattern. Compare each expected output with the code before changing it.

examples.expectedOutput: add inserts a single element into the set.
A set cannot contain duplicate equal elements.
update adds each element from the iterable.
update accepts multiple iterables and adds their elements.
examples.explanation: Add a tuple as one element

examples.expectedOutput: A tuple of hashable values can itself be a set member.
